title: The Antique Collector Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention, including the final scene where Suwa attacks Kogoro after being exposed -- that beat has no non-recurring-cast participants so it is not representable as an edge under this convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. Maru held both Suwa's and Akutsu's valuables as loan collateral; Suwa's true motive (secretly selling the pawned family sword after threatening to kill Maru if he did) and Akutsu's near-identical red-herring motive (unpaid debt + an almost identical threat over his own pawned carving) are intentionally parallel in the transcript, which is what makes Akutsu a strong false suspect before the answering-machine-tape and dying-message evidence resolve it onto Suwa.

attrs.died_of: single sword strike during a fight in his cottage
attrs.lending_practice: held valuables (a family heirloom sword, a wood carving) from acquaintances as collateral against loans he made them

attrs.secret: having an affair with Dr. Hatano; paid Kogoro Mouri extra to keep the affair he was hired to investigate quiet

attrs.tell: small scar between thumb and index finger from sword-sheathing practice, marking him as an expert swordsman
attrs.claimed_alibi: says he was meditating alone at his dojo between 3:00 and 5:00, with no one to verify it
says he was at a movie theater in Ginza at 3:00, alone
says he was alone at his studio between 3:00 and 5:00
attrs.false_suspicion: wrongly accused mid-episode: the staged sword-grip flaw and his own untouched carving made him look like the killer, and he told the truth about leaving a phone message that nobody could initially verify

attrs.role_in_case: murder scene; kept separate from the main house so Maru could meet visitors privately

attrs.staging_flaw: found positioned backwards in the victim's hands relative to a photo taken earlier -- proves someone repositioned it after death

attrs.description: Suwa family heirloom sword, passed down for generations
attrs.history: left with Maru as collateral against a loan; Maru secretly sold it despite Suwa's explicit threat to kill him if he did

attrs.description: Akutsu's own work, left with Maru as collateral against a 10-million-yen loan
attrs.anomaly: the only object in the cottage left undamaged amid an otherwise thoroughly sword-slashed room

attrs.original_content: Akutsu's genuine call, made shortly before 4:00, about the loan and his threatened carving -- it rang many times unanswered because the killer was mid-murder, then rolled to the machine
attrs.tampering: rewound and recorded over by Suwa, erasing Akutsu's message and replacing it with Suwa's own message claiming he'd arrive earlier than his 6:00 appointment

attrs.dying_message: Maru, dying, carved "Suwa" into the drawers with the murder sword
attrs.tampering: Suwa discovered the message, physically swapped several drawers out of order, and added extra sword cuts on top to scramble the carved name
attrs.staging_flaw: the large sword cuts covering the room don't connect across the swapped drawers -- the pattern only makes sense once the drawers are moved back to their original positions, revealing "Suwa" again

attrs.content: lists four visitors scheduled for the day of the murder: Kogoro Mouri, Yuji Suwa, Ikuya Hatano, and Makoto Akutsu

clues.desc: A photo taken candidly of the crime scene shows the murder sword held one way in the victim's hands; by the time the body was formally examined the grip was reversed -- proves someone repositioned the sword post-mortem, which points at whoever staged the scene rather than whoever actually fought Maru.

Of three phone calls placed to the Maru residence that afternoon, two rang once and stopped (callers who got through and hung up or left quickly); the earliest, placed before 4:00, rang on and on before finally rolling to the answering machine -- timestamps the murder to that window, since only someone busy committing it would fail to pick up for that long.

edges.detail: sold the pawned Kikuchiyo sword instead of returning it, breaking his promise to Suwa
waits in the main house while her husband receives his visitor in the cottage, and orders the housekeepers to fetch him when he doesn't return
confronts Maru over secretly selling the pawned Kikuchiyo heirloom sword despite Suwa's earlier threat

edges.method: cut down with Maru's own decorative katana, taken from the cottage alcove, during a sword fight

edges.detail: dying, Maru carves "Suwa" into the drawer chest with the murder sword as a dying message
calls the Maru residence about the loan and his threatened carving; the phone rings unanswered for a long time because Suwa is mid-murder, and the call rolls to the answering machine
rewinds the answering machine tape and records his own message over Akutsu's, erasing the evidence that Akutsu called and faking that he himself would arrive earlier than planned
discovers the dying message, swaps drawers out of order, and adds new sword cuts to scramble the carved name "Suwa"
slashes walls, ceiling, and furniture throughout the cottage so the drawer damage doesn't stand out as singled out
places the sword backwards in the victim's hands so the scene will look like someone else tried to frame him, giving himself a built-in escape route

edges.motive_type: unpaid_debt_and_near-identical_threat_over_his_own_pawned_carving (red herring -- prime suspect for most of the episode due to staged evidence)
